subject: Materials Science
title: Autoclave Curing: Aerospace Precision
description: A micro-lesson that makes Autoclave Curing: Aerospace Precision usable.

hook.text: A giant pressure cooker the size of a bus bakes carbon fiber parts at 180°C and 7 atmospheres.

buildup.text: Autoclaves apply heat and pressure simultaneously — squeezing out voids and curing resin perfectly.

discovery.text: The result is void content below 1% — the gold standard for aerospace-grade composites.

twist.text: Autoclaves cost millions and each cure cycle takes hours — slow, expensive, and energy-hungry.

climax.text: Boeing 787 wing skins cure in autoclaves large enough to park an aircraft inside.

punchline.text: Pressure plus heat equals perfection — at a price.

quiz.question: Why do aerospace composites require autoclave curing?
options: It is the cheapest curing method
High pressure and heat minimize voids for maximum strength
